method: Independent static review of the exact line-2052 declaration, its complete current verify-test-runtime-v3 source-input union, the closed Stage 22/24 operation registry and app/worker/store/engine caller graph, the separately inventoried external-response entrypoints, and the independently expected positive, failure, retry and command-vocabulary assertions of test-ir.native-stale-recovery and test-ir.native-canonical-identity. The source graph and payload contracts establish that registered application-native results use only the direct native-result command and do not enter external capture, validation, attachment, proposal, acceptance, rejection, abandonment or human-input routes. This review establishes declaration completeness before execution; a current eligible default-owner receipt and canonical aggregation/readback remain separately required before the declaration can yield CONFORMANT_PROVEN.

additionalControllingContext.meaning: Supplies the pronoun antecedent: application-native deterministic results. It remains a separate requirement and is not claimed complete by this review.

independentlyExpectedOutcomes: The Stage 22 RUN_NATIVE_TESTS and Stage 24 RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS registry rows are APPLICATION, DIRECT_COMMAND, acceptsExternalResponse false, expose no response types, and permit no external writable fields.

The actual app handler executes the isolated Test IR worker and dispatches nativeProductResults through persistReplacement to commitNativeProductResults without creating replacementReview or any raw-response/proposal state.

The native command vocabulary accepts only job, stage, runtime results, exact input identities, revision/state identity and history view; wrong stage, duplicate test, caller project candidates, caller mutation confirmation, stale identity and malformed batches reject atomically.
A failed native write preserves stored state and retains the exact uncommitted observations for one retry without another worker execution; an uncertain outcome is not replayed.
The separately enumerated external-response APIs remain a disjoint caller and payload graph; no fabricated execution of those unrelated APIs is required to prove the bypass route.
